title: Webb's First Deep Field
caption: Galaxy cluster SMACS 0723, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESA/Webb press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Thousands of galaxies crowd this small patch of sky, among them the faintest objects ever seen in infrared light. This is Webb's First Deep Field, the image that introduced the telescope to the world, and it centers on the galaxy cluster SMACS 0723.

The whole frame covers a piece of sky about the size of a grain of sand held at arm's length. The cluster itself appears as it was 4.6 billion years ago, and its combined mass works as a gravitational lens, bending and magnifying the light of galaxies far behind it. Those are the stretched arcs and smears scattered through the picture.

Webb's Near-Infrared Camera built the image from exposures at several wavelengths totaling 12.5 hours, and reached deeper in infrared than Hubble's deepest fields, which took weeks. It resolves tiny star clusters and faint structures inside the lensed galaxies, the start of Webb's search for the earliest galaxies in the universe.

understand.summary: Webb's NIRCam combined six filters from 0.9 to 4.4 microns, with the shorter wavelengths shown in blue and green and the longest in orange and red.
understand.eye: Almost all of this light is infrared, invisible to the eye; the colors translate it into visible hues.
